title: Import tariff on domestic firm investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects).
- Why: A clearly defined treated group (U.S. steel/metals producers) experiences a policy shock (2018 steel/aluminum tariffs) at a common time, with a suitable control group (non-metals manufacturers). Panel data over multiple pre/post quarters enables controlling for time-invariant firm heterogeneity and common time shocks.
- Estimation: y_it = β DID · (treated_i × post_t) + α_i + γ_t + ε_it, with unit and period fixed effects and standard errors clustered at the firm level.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the tariff, treated and control firms would have had parallel trends in log capex.
  - No spillovers: Control firms are not indirectly affected by the tariff in a way that differentially changes their investment path relative to treated firms.
  - Stable composition/no differential sorting over time.
  - Common treatment timing and no anticipation (checked with an event-study pre-trend test).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# 0) Setup and read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s06_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Ensure variables are properly typed
df$unit_id <- as.integer(df$unit_id)
df$period  <- as.integer(df$period)
df$treated <- as.integer(df$treated)
df$post    <- as.integer(df$post)
if (!"treat_x_post" %in% names(df)) {
  df$treat_x_post <- df$treated * df$post
}

# Helper: clustered SEs (unit level) if sandwich/lmtest are available
have_sandwich <- requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)
have_lmtest   <- requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)

get_ct <- function(mod, cluster_formula = ~ unit_id) {
  if (have_sandwich && have_lmtest) {
    vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(mod, cluster = cluster_formula, type = "HC1")
    ct <- lmtest::coeftest(mod, vcov. = vc)
    return(list(ct = ct, vc = vc, robust = TRUE))
  } else {
    ct <- summary(mod)$coef
    return(list(ct = ct, vc = vcov(mod), robust = FALSE))
  }
}

# 1) Main DID: unit and time FE, cluster-robust SEs at unit level
did_mod <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
did_res <- get_ct(did_mod)

# Extract main coefficient
coef_name <- "treat_x_post"
if (!(coef_name %in% rownames(did_res$ct))) {
  stop("Coefficient treat_x_post not found in model results.")
}
beta_hat <- as.numeric(did_res$ct[coef_name, "Estimate"])
se_hat   <- as.numeric(did_res$ct[coef_name, "Std. Error"])
t_stat   <- as.numeric(did_res$ct[coef_name, "t value"])
p_val    <- as.numeric(did_res$ct[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])

# 95% CI using normal approx (robust or not, same quantile)
z <- 1.96
ci_lo <- beta_hat - z * se_hat
ci_hi <- beta_hat + z * se_hat

cat("Main DID estimate (treated x post):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-value = %.4g\n",
            beta_hat, se_hat, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_val))
if (did_res$robust) {
  cat("  SEs: Cluster-robust at firm (unit) level (HC1).\n\n")
} else {
  cat("  SEs: Conventional (sandwich/lmtest not available).\n\n")
}

# 2) Event-study (dynamic effects) with unit and time FE; base period: event time = -1
# Tariff effective at period = 4 => event time = period - 4
df$rel_time <- df$period - 4
# Set the -1 quarter as the omitted baseline
df$rel_time_f <- factor(df$rel_time)
if (!("-1" %in% levels(df$rel_time_f))) {
  # If missing (should not happen), set nearest pre as baseline
  # But in these data, periods are 1..8 => rel_time in -3..4, so -1 exists.
  warning("Baseline event time -1 not in data; using the first available pre-period as baseline.")
}
df$rel_time_f <- stats::relevel(df$rel_time_f, ref = "-1")

es_mod <- lm(y ~ treated:rel_time_f + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
es_res <- get_ct(es_mod)

# Extract event-time interaction coefficients and SEs
all_terms <- rownames(es_res$ct)
es_terms <- grep("^treated:rel_time_f", all_terms, value = TRUE)

extract_k <- function(x) {
  # term names like "treated:rel_time_f-3"
  as.numeric(sub("treated:rel_time_f", "", x))
}
ks <- sapply(es_terms, extract_k)
ord <- order(ks)
ks <- ks[ord]
es_beta <- es_res$ct[es_terms, , drop = FALSE][ord, , drop = FALSE]

# Print event-study estimates (relative to t = -1)
cat("Event-study coefficients (relative to t = -1), with unit & time FE:\n")
for (i in seq_along(ks)) {
  k <- ks[i]
  b <- as.numeric(es_beta[i, "Estimate"])
  s <- as.numeric(es_beta[i, "Std. Error"])
  pv <- as.numeric(es_beta[i, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  cat(sprintf("  k = %2d: beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4g\n", k, b, s, pv))
}
if (es_res$robust) {
  cat("  SEs: Cluster-robust at firm (unit) level (HC1).\n\n")
} else {
  cat("  SEs: Conventional (sandwich/lmtest not available).\n\n")
}

# 3) Placebo DID on pre-periods only (no true treatment yet)
pre_df <- subset(df, period <= 3)
pre_df$fake_post <- as.integer(pre_df$period >= 3)  # placebo at last pre quarter
pre_df$fake_treat_post <- pre_df$treated * pre_df$fake_post

placebo_mod <- lm(y ~ fake_treat_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = pre_df)
placebo_res <- get_ct(placebo_mod)

p_name <- "fake_treat_post"
if (p_name %in% rownames(placebo_res$ct)) {
  p_b <- as.numeric(placebo_res$ct[p_name, "Estimate"])
  p_s <- as.numeric(placebo_res$ct[p_name, "Std. Error"])
  p_p <- as.numeric(placebo_res$ct[p_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  cat("Placebo DID (pre-periods only; fake post at period >= 3):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p-value = %.4g\n\n", p_b, p_s, p_p))
}

# 4) Robustness: Add unit-specific linear trends
df$t <- as.numeric(df$period)
trend_mod <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period) + factor(unit_id):t, data = df)
trend_res <- get_ct(trend_mod)

if (coef_name %in% rownames(trend_res$ct)) {
  tb <- as.numeric(trend_res$ct[coef_name, "Estimate"])
  tsd <- as.numeric(trend_res$ct[coef_name, "Std. Error"])
  tpv <- as.numeric(trend_res$ct[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  cat("DID with unit-specific linear trends:\n")
  cat(sprintf("  beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p-value = %.4g\n", tb, tsd, tpv))
  if (trend_res$robust) {
    cat("  SEs: Cluster-robust at firm (unit) level (HC1).\n")
  } else {
    cat("  SEs: Conventional (sandwich/lmtest not available).\n")
  }
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. The tariff likely raised domestic steel prices/margins, easing internal funds and improving expected returns on capacity expansion, increasing capex among steel producers relative to other manufacturers.
- Magnitude: On log capex, an increase of roughly 0.10–0.20 log points (≈10–20%) for treated firms post-2018Q1 versus controls, with insignificant pre-trends in the event study and a null placebo. The trend-augmented model should yield a similar positive but possibly attenuated estimate.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=protected sector firms, control=unaffected manufacturers
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Tariff-protected firms increase capex relative to non-protected peers
_ground_truth.main_effect: 22% higher investment in treated firms post-tariff
